claims.text: A strong low-field magnetocaloric response together with rapid heat exchange, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability is governed by a single-phase solid solution with moderate lattice distortion and high electronic or magnetic entropy change near the magnetic transition.
The proposed single-phase state promotes a sharp, reversible magnetic transition.
The proposed single-phase state suppresses phase separation or martensitic transformations.
Phase separation or martensitic transformations increase hysteresis and degrade mechanical properties.
The initial material is a rare-earth-free, FeMnCoNi-based HEA in a homogenized single-phase solid-solution state.
Partial replacement of Ni with Cu or Cr can be used to vary lattice distortion while retaining overall phase stability.
Moderate lattice distortion enhances magnetic entropy change by promoting cooperative spin alignment.
Moderate lattice distortion sharpens the magnetic transition.
Suppressing structural transitions reduces hysteresis and mechanical instability.
Excessive lattice distortion or phase separation reduces the magnetocaloric effect.
Excessive lattice distortion or phase separation degrades mechanical properties.
Moderately distorted, single-phase alloys will exhibit larger isothermal magnetic entropy change and adiabatic temperature change at low fields than highly distorted or multiphase alloys.
Moderately distorted, single-phase alloys will exhibit less thermal and magnetic hysteresis than highly distorted or multiphase alloys.
Moderately distorted, single-phase alloys will exhibit greater mechanical stability than highly distorted or multiphase alloys.
The hypothesis is expected to hold for rare-earth-free, single-phase FCC or BCC HEAs with atomic-size mismatch below approximately 6% and applied magnetic fields below 1 T.
The hypothesis may not apply to multiphase alloys, alloys undergoing martensitic transitions, or measurements at very high applied fields.
The optimal degree of lattice distortion may depend on the specific alloy chemistry.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis attributes the desired combined performance partly to rapid heat exchange, but neither the predicted outcomes nor the baseline comparison specifies any heat-transfer variable or prediction. Thus the rapid-heat-exchange portion is not carried through the proposed causal test.
